set_aside.subject: list-record and page-filter discriminator types
set_aside.text: “a table keyed by the record type and total over its members, and a relation between record types and filter fields” and “It accepts no table name, SQL fragment, untyped payload or path.”
set_aside.question: Which module owns the closed typed representations of a listable record type and its filter fields, so `surface`, `store`, and `store_persistence` do not invent incompatible strings or query types?
options: Add record-type and filter-field discriminators to `models`
Let `data_provider` define both the types and their allowed relation
Define separate typed paging operations in `store` for every permitted record/filter pair
set_aside.default_guess: Define the discriminators in `models`, with `data_provider` owning only the allowed record-type/filter-field relation.

set_aside.subject: page-query lowering dependency
set_aside.text: `data_provider` owns “LISTABLE_RECORD_TYPES” and “PAGE_FILTERS”, while `store_persistence` provides operations “for a listed record type” and hides “which column each filter field of a page compares”; both modules are on the same dependency line and “modules on one line do not know each other.”
set_aside.question: How does `store_persistence` learn which record types and filter fields require page statements without depending on `data_provider` or independently repeating the policy values it owns?
options: Allow `store_persistence` to depend on `data_provider` by placing it later in the dependency order
Pass a generated paging specification into both modules from a named non-runtime owner
Make `store_persistence` support a policy-independent typed superset, with `surface`/`store` restricting it through `data_provider`
set_aside.default_guess: Make `store_persistence` expose a policy-independent typed superset and have `surface` and `store` apply the `data_provider` allowlist.
